subject: Realtime output hiccup during peak - urgent exec briefing
messages:
From: Annie Liao <annie.liao@brightleaf.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime output stalls since 09:00 PDT

Hi Alex,

We're seeing a severe regression on our integration this morning. Starting ~09:00 PDT our clients report repeated stalls in the realtime stream: partial chunks that never complete, then a hard client error (504 / upstream timeout) after ~20s. Throughput dropped by roughly 30% and P95 latency for tokens jumped from 120ms to ~520ms. Error rate on our side is ~12% for streaming sessions.

Attached is a short trace and a screenshot from our frontend showing the stalled chunk. I can reproduce in our test harness (attached logs). This is customer-impacting — several paying users are affected. Can you triage and advise immediate mitigations (fallbacks, rate limit, config)?

Attachments: streaming_trace_20270612.log (text), brightleaf_screenshot_0612.png (image)

Thanks,
Annie
Head of Integrations, Brightleaf
annie.liao@brightleaf.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Annie Liao <annie.liao@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime output stalls since 09:00 PDT

Hi Annie — thanks for the quick report and the logs. I'm escalating to infra and the realtime team now (cc'ed). Initial plan:

- Short-term mitigation: enable HTTP chunked fallback for affected sessions and reduce client-side max idle to 10s.
- Mid-term: route Brightleaf traffic to a dedicated routing pool to avoid noisy neighbors while we triage.
- We need the full server-side websocket traces (ws frames + keepalive) if you have them.

Laura / Rishi — can you pick this up? Please share a quick action plan and ETA.

Alex
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime output stalls since 09:00 PDT

Thanks Alex / Annie — I'm looking at the traces now. Quick findings:

- Correlation with traffic burst: spike at 09:02 - 09:08 where concurrent streaming connections for Brightleaf jumped ~5.8x over baseline.
- Observed symptoms: intermittent WS ping timeouts, repeated chunked transfer pauses, upstream NGINX 504s on the stream termination path.
- Error surface: client-side reported 524/504 + internal gateway 499 on some torn connections.

Immediate actions taken (09:35):
- Flipped "enable_chunked_fallback=true" for Brightleaf in routing config.
- Temporarily applied per-customer concurrency cap: 20 connections per IP to smooth bursts.
- Dumped worker logs and captured sample frames (attached: nginx_504_samples.txt, streaming_trace_20270612.log).

Suggested next steps (ETA listed):
1) Route Brightleaf to reserved pool (2 GPU workers) to isolate noisy traffic — ETA 2h for policy rollout.
2) Increase WebSocket keepalive and reduce idle timeout from 45s -> 15s; will push a config in 45m.
3) If incidents persist, failover to an older model variant with lower memory footprint for long responses — prep in 1.5h.

Annie: please confirm whether the affected requests are long-form generation (>1024 tokens) or standard convo length. That will change our rollback strategy.

Laura
Principal CS Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime output stalls since 09:00 PDT

Update from infra side:

Root-candidate: sudden burst behavior is overflowing our per-worker frame queues under the default continuous-batching window, creating backpressure on the chunk emitter. When the emitter's buffer hits the threshold it stalls and the client sees a partial chunk that never completes. NGINX times out connections that linger waiting for final chunk.

Planned mitigations (I will execute in this order):
- 10:30: reduce max_batch_window from 120ms -> 60ms for the Brightleaf route (low risk).
- 11:15: increase emitter buffer watermark by 30% (will require rolling restart of the websocket-worker group).
- 13:00 UTC (~06:00 PDT): scheduled rolling restart of one worker cluster to clear existing hung state; we will do it in a staggered fashion to avoid downtime.
- If residual errors >5% after these changes, we will cut traffic to the dedicated reserved pool (estimated 30min to move route).

I also pushed an internal Grafana panel for Brightleaf traffic: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-health?orgId=1&var-account=Brightleaf (read-only).

Note: these changes may temporarily increase token-unit cost due to lower batching efficiency; estimate +8-12% until we stabilize.

Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime

Marissa / Monica — looping you in for visibility and approval on a short mitigation spend. Summary below:

What happened:
- At ~09:02 PDT Brightleaf traffic experienced burst that led to WS emitter buffer backpressure and partial chunk stalls; clients hit 504/524.
- Impact: ~12% streaming error rate for Brightleaf, throughput -30% at peak, token P95 increased to ~520ms. Active impacted users: a small cohort of paying customers (we have session ids).

What we changed so far:
- Enabled chunked-fallback and applied a temporary per-IP concurrency cap (done).
- Reduced batch window and will increase emitter watermark; scheduled rolling restart to clear hung workers.

Options requiring exec approval now:
1) Provision 2 hours of dedicated reserved pool capacity (estimate cost $12,000) to isolate Brightleaf while we confirm root cause and harden configs. This will reduce risk of recurrence and buy time for a proper fix.
2) Issue a one-time $5k credit to Brightleaf for immediate customer remediation communication (they asked for goodwill).

Request: Approve option 1 (temporary reserved capacity) and optionally 2. We expect mitigation time <6 hours after the reserved pool switch.

If approved, I'll proceed with the routing change and send a customer-facing status note.

Alex Martinez
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
